Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:1.english: The homeborn - [As in the verse:] “...among the children of Israel shall reside in sukkot.”

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:2.hebrew: אזרח זה אזרח - אי הוה כתיב אזרח, הוי משמע כל תולדות ישראל — אנשים ונשים:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:2.english: “Homeborn” — this is a homeborn - Had it been written [simply] “homeborn,” it would imply all descendants of Israel — men and women.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:3.hebrew: כתיב האזרח - מיומן שבאזרחים, להוציא את הנשים:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:3.english: It is written: “The homeborn” - The select among the homeborn, to exclude women.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:10:4.english: To include the minors - Later on, we raise a contradiction from a baraita against it.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:11:1.hebrew: בעינוי - יום הכפורים, דכתיב: "תענו את נפשותיכם וכל מלאכה לא תעשו האזרח והגר", אלמא ה' לרבויי אתא:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:11:1.english: In affliction - [That of] Yom Kippur, as it is written: “You shall afflict your souls, and shall do no manner of work, the homeborn, or the stranger” (Leviticus 16:29); evidently, the [letter] heh comes to include.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:11:2.hebrew: אמר רבה הלכתא נינהו ואסמכינהו רבנן אקראי - הנך תרי מילי ליכא למידרשינהו לתרוייהו מקראי, דאם זו ה' לרבות — אף זו ה' לרבות, ואם זו למעט — אף זו למעט. אלא על פי הלכה שנאמרה למשה מסיני באחד מהן, לחילוף נאמרו שני דברים הללו — זו לחיוב וזו לפטור; וחדא מינייהו לאו ממשמעותא, אלא רבנן אסמכינהו אקראי: חדא ממשמעותא, וחדא אסמכתא בעלמא, דאלו קרא חילופא משמע, ולמילתא אחריתי אתא:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:11:2.english: Rabba said: They are a halakha, and the Sages supported them with verses - These two matters cannot both be derived from the verses, for if this [letter] heh is to include, this [other letter] heh too is to include; and if this [one] is to exclude, this [one] too is to exclude. Rather, based on a halakha that was transmitted to Moses from Sinai regarding one of them, these two matters were stated in opposite ways — this one for obligation and that one for exemption. And one of them is not from the [actual] implication [of the verse]; rather, the Sages supported them on the verses: one is from the [actual] implication, and one is merely a support [asmakhta], for the verse implies the opposite, and came for another matter.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:12:1.hebrew: ה"ג: הי קרא והי הלכתא, ותו למה לי קרא למה לי הלכתא - הי קרא: הי מינייהו ממשמעותא, והי לאו ממשמעותא דקרא — דאלו קרא חילופא משמע, אלא מהלכתא הוא דאתמר? ותו, למה לי קרא למה לי הלכתא: לא בסוכה לפטור, ולא בעינוי לחיוב:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:12:1.english: This is the correct reading: Which is the verse and which is the halakha? And furthermore, why do I need a verse, why do I need a halakha? - “Which is the verse?”: Which of them is derived from the [literal] meaning [of the verse], and which is not from the meaning of the verse — since the verse implies the opposite, but rather it was stated as a halakha? “And furthermore, why do I need a verse, why do I need a halakha?”: Neither in [the case of] sukka to exempt [women], nor in [the case of] affliction [on Yom Kippur] to obligate [them].

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:12:2.hebrew: נשים פטורות - בפ"ק דקדושין (ד' לד.) מפרש:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:12:2.english: Women are exempt - [The Gemara] explains [this] in the first chapter of Kiddushin (daf 34a).

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:13:1.hebrew: ויום הכפורים - לא תעשה הוא, וכרת הוא. וכל מצות לא תעשה — בין זמן גרמא בין לא זמן גרמא — נפקא לן בקדושין (ד' לה.) מדרב יהודה דחייבות:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:13:1.english: And Yom Kippur - It is a negative commandment, and it [involves] karet. And all negative commandments — whether time-bound or not time-bound — we derive in Kiddushin (35a) from [the teaching of] Rav Yehuda that [women] are obligated.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:1:1.hebrew: התם מבטל ליה - להאי פקק לגבי חלון, וחשיב ליה מכותל עצמו, הלכך הוי מוסיף. אבל סדין, אנן סהדי דלא מבטיל ליה לגבי סוכה, וסופו ליטלו; הלכך, לא פשיטא לרבי אליעזר דליהוי מוסיף:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:1:1.english: There, he negates it - [Namely,] this shutter relative to the window, and considers it [part of] the wall itself; therefore, it is [considered] adding [to a structure]. But [with regard to] a sheet, we are witnesses that he does not negate it relative to the sukkah, and he will ultimately remove it; therefore, it was not obvious to Rabbi Eliezer that it should be [considered] adding.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:3:1.english: [Are] only from what you heard - [This was said] in astonishment [as a question].

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:3:2.hebrew: הזקקתוני - כלומר, תזקיקוני לומר דבר כו' — אגיד לכם את מדותי, וזו אחת מהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:3:2.english: You forced me - That is to say: You compel me to say a matter, etc. — I will tell you my practices, and this is one of them.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:3:3.hebrew: שיחת חולין - דברי הבאי ושחוק. כלומר, מה שספק בידי — לא מפני (שטרחתי) בכל אלה; ואי אפשר שאמרו רבותי דבר בבית המדרש ולא שמעתיו, ומה שלא שמעתי לא אומר, שכך היא מדתי:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:3:3.english: Idle conversation - Words of nonsense and jesting. That is to say: that which is in doubt to me [is] not because (I troubled myself) in all these [matters]; and it is impossible that my teachers said a thing in the study hall and I did not hear it; and that which I did not hear, I do not say, for such is my practice.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:4:1.hebrew: בלא תורה - בלא גירסא, שהיה הולך ושונה תמיד:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:4:1.english: Without Torah - Without recitation, for he was always walking and studying.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:4:2.hebrew: חוץ מערבי פסחים - מפני עשיית פסחיהם, ומפני התינוקות שלא ישנו. כך מפורש בפסחים (דף קט.):
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:4:2.english: Except on Passover eves - Because of the preparation of their Paschal offerings, and because of the children, so that they will not fall asleep. So it is explained in Pesachim (daf 109a).

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:4:3.english: And the eve of Yom Kippur - For one must eat while it is still day.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:1.english: Mishnah - Such as the Mishnah and the Baraita of the Six Orders.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:10.english: The conversation of ministering angels, the conversation of demons, the conversation of palm trees - I do not know what it is.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:11.hebrew: משלות כובסין ומשלות שועלים - שיסדו קדמונים לתת אמתלא לתוכחתם, ותולין אותן בכובסים ובשועלים, כגון (סנהדרין לט.): מאזני צדק, אבות אכלו בוסר:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:11.english: Parables of launderers and parables of foxes - Which the ancients composed to provide a pretext for their rebuke, and they attribute them to launderers and to foxes; such as [those cited in] (Sanhedrin 39a): "Just balances," [and] "The fathers have eaten sour grapes."

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:2.hebrew: גמרא - זו היא סברא, שהיו התנאים אחרונים מדקדקים בדברי הראשונים הסתומים לפרשם וליתן בהן טעם, כמו שעשו האמוראים אחר התנאים, שפירשו דברי התנאים שלפניהן וקבעו בהן גמרא; ואותו דיוק שבימי התנאי' נקרא הש"ס:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:2.english: Gemara - This refers to reasoning that the later Tannaim would analyze in the obscure statements of the earlier ones to explain them and provide a reason for them, just as the Amoraim did after the Tannaim, explaining the statements of the Tannaim who preceded them and establishing Gemara based on them; and that analysis from the time of the Tannaim was called the Shas.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:3.hebrew: הלכות - הלכה למשה מסיני, כגון: גוד, ולבוד, ודופן עקומה; שיעורין, חציצין, מחיצין; עשר נטיעות, ערבה, וניסוך המים:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:3.english: Halakhot - Halakhah transmitted to Moses from Sinai, such as: gud [extend], and lavud, and a curved wall [dofen akumah]; measurements, interpositions [in immersion], [and] partitions; ten saplings, [the] willow [branch], and the water libation.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:4.hebrew: דקדוקי תורה - ריבויי אותיות שבאין לדרוש בהן ריבוים ומעוטים, כגון האזרח להוציא הנשים — שדקדקה התורה בלשונה לכתוב אות יתירה ללמד:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:4.english: Minutiae of the Torah - Additional letters from which [the Sages] come to expound inclusions and exclusions, such as Ha'ezraḥ ["the native"] to exclude women — where the Torah was meticulous in its wording to write an extra letter to teach [a law].

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:5.hebrew: דקדוקי סופרים - שהוסיפו לדקדק אחר מעשה הבריות, ולהחמיר, ולעשות סייג ואזנים לתורה, וגזרו גזרות להרחיק את האדם מן העבירה. ודכוותה בבכורות (ד' ל:): גר הבא לקבל תורה עליו חוץ מדבר אחד — אין מקבלין אותו; ר' יוסי אומר: אפילו דקדוק אחד מדקדוקי סופרים:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:5.english: Minutiae of the scribes - That they added scrutiny regarding the conduct of people, and [saw fit] to be stringent and to make a fence and handles for the Torah, and they enacted decrees to distance a person from transgression. And similar to this is in Bekhorot (daf 30b): A convert who comes to accept the Torah upon himself except for one matter, they do not accept him; Rabbi Yosei says: Even one detail of the minutiae of the scribes.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:6.hebrew: קלים וחמורים - דברים הלמדין בק"ו, שניתנו לדון מעצמן לכל אדם, ולא פירשו כלום בסיני:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:6.english: A fortiori inferences - Matters that are derived through an a fortiori inference, which were given to any person to deduce on their own, and nothing [of them] was explicitly specified at Sinai.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:7.hebrew: וגזרות שוות - דברים הלמדין בג"ש:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:7.english: And verbal analogies - Matters that are derived through a verbal analogy.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:8.english: Seasons - The calculation of the movement of the sun and the moon.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:9.hebrew: וגימטריאות - דברים הלמדין בלשון גימטריא, כגון (ירמיהו כה) שש"ך — בבל בא"ת ב"ש, כשדים (שם נא) — לב קמי בא"ת ב"ש, סהדה מנון (לקמן סוכה ד' נב:) — בא"ט ב"ח; וכן לפי מנין האותיות, כגון: סתם נזירות שלשים יום (נזיר ד' ה.) מקדוש יהיה — יהי"ה בגימטריא שלשים הוו:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:6:9.english: And numerology [gimmatreyaot] - Matters that are learned through the medium of gematria, such as (Jeremiah 25[:26]) Sheshakh [which is] Babel in atbash; [and for] Kasdim (ibid. 51[:1]), "lev kamai" in atbash; [and that] a witness [sahada is called] "manon" (below, Sukkah 52b) in atbach. And likewise according to the numerical count of the letters, such as an unspecified Nazirite vow [being] thirty days (Nazir 5a), from "he shall be holy [kadosh yihyeh]" (Numbers 6:5) — [the letters of] Y-H-Y-H in gematria are thirty.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:7:1.hebrew: הויות דאביי ורבא - כל איבעי' להו לאביי ורבא, הוה מספקא להו; ובכולן נתן את לבו ונתן בהן טעם, ובימי אמוראים נשתכחו:
Rashi on Sukkah 28a:7:1.english: The discussions of Abaye and Rava - Every inquiry of Abaye and Rava was in doubt to them; and regarding all of them, [Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai] applied his mind and provided a rationale for them, but in the days of the Amoraim they were forgotten.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:7:2.english: Was incinerated - For the ministering angels would gather around him to hear words of Torah from his mouth.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:8:1.english: Is there proof from there? - [This is stated] as a question.

Rashi on Sukkah 28a:9:1.english: Women and slaves - [The reason is] explained in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Sukkah 28a:11:1.hebrew: הלכתא נינהו - "הלכתא היא" גרסינן, לשון יחיד — דחדא מינייהו הלכתא, ותו לא. ובריש בנות כותים (נדה דף לב.) גבי "אין לי אלא אשה", נקט לשון רבים, לפי שמסופק על שניהם: הי מינייהו הלכתא:
Tosafot on Sukkah 28a:11:1.english: "They are a halakha" - We read: "It is a halakha," in the singular, for [only] one of them is a halakha, and no more. And at the beginning of [the chapter] Benot Kutim (Niddah 32a), regarding "I only have [a verse for] a woman," [the Gemara] employs the plural phrasing, because it is in doubt regarding both of them [as to] which of them is the halakha.

Tosafot on Sukkah 28a:7:1.hebrew: כל עוף שפורח עליו מיד נשרף - שהדברים שמחים כנתינתם בסיני, שנתנה תורה באש. וכענין זה מצינו במדרש בעובדא דרבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע, שהיו מסובין בסעודה וליהטה האש סביבם:
Tosafot on Sukkah 28a:7:1.english: Any bird that flew over him was immediately incinerated - For the words [of Torah] were as joyous as when they were given at Sinai, since the Torah was given in fire. And along these lines, we find in the Midrash regarding the incident of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who were reclining at a banquet and fire blazed around them.
